simplex method.definition: An iterative algorithm for solving linear programming problems by moving from one feasible solution to another with a better objective function value until an optimal solution is found.

klee-minty cube.definition: A specific linear programming problem designed to demonstrate the worst-case exponential time complexity of the simplex method.

largest coefficient rule.definition: A pivot rule in the simplex method that selects the variable with the largest coefficient in the objective function to enter the basis.

smallest coefficient rule.definition: A pivot rule in the simplex method that selects the variable with the smallest coefficient in the objective function to enter the basis.

efficiency of simplex method.definition: Analyzing the average and worst-case performance of the simplex method, particularly in terms of the number of iterations required for convergence.

worst-case example.definition: Constructing a specific linear programming problem (Klee-Minty cube) that forces the simplex method to take an exponential number of steps.

impact of pivot rules.definition: Demonstrating how different pivot rules (Largest Coefficient Rule vs. Smallest Coefficient Rule) can drastically affect the number of iterations required by the simplex method, especially in worst-case scenarios.

transforming a linear program through si.term: Transforming a linear program through simplex iterations
transforming a linear program through si.definition: This involves modifying the objective function, constraint matrix, and right-hand side vector of a linear program during the iterative process of the simplex method.

simplex iteration.definition: $\overline{A} = T A$, $\overline{b} = T b$, $\overline{c}^T = c^T - y^T A$, $\overline{j} = y^T b$, where $T$ is a transformation matrix, and $y$ is a vector related to the dual variables.

slack variables.definition: Variables added to convert inequality constraints into equality constraints in a linear program.

cost vector.definition: A vector representing the coefficients of the decision variables in the objective function of a linear program.

constraint matrix.definition: A matrix containing the coefficients of the decision variables in the constraints of a linear program.

right-hand side vector.definition: A vector containing the constant values on the right-hand side of the constraints in a linear program.

decision variables.definition: The variables in a linear program that represent the quantities to be determined in order to optimize the objective function.

representing a linear program in matrix.term: Representing a linear program in matrix form
representing a linear program in matrix.definition: This involves expressing the objective function, constraints, and variables of a linear program using matrices and vectors.

convex set.definition: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ is convex if for any two points $z_1, z_2 \in S$, the line segment connecting them, defined by $tz_1 + (1-t)z_2$ where $0 < t < 1$, is entirely contained within $S$.

convex combination.definition: A convex combination of points $z_1, z_2, \dots, z_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ is a weighted sum of the form $t_1 z_1 + t_2 z_2 + \dots + t_n z_n$, where $t_i \ge 0$ for all $i$ and $\sum_i t_i = 1$.

theorem 10.1.definition: A set $S$ is convex if and only if it contains all convex combinations of its points.

convex set verification.definition: Determining whether a given set satisfies the definition of a convex set, i.e., if the line segment connecting any two points in the set is entirely contained within the set.

convex combination membership.definition: Determining whether a given point can be expressed as a convex combination of other points within a set.

equivalence of convexity and convex comb.term: Equivalence of Convexity and Convex Combinations
equivalence of convexity and convex comb.definition: Proving that a set is convex if and only if it contains all convex combinations of its points.

production planning.definition: The process of determining the most efficient way to meet demand for a product over a given time period, considering factors like production capacity, inventory, and costs.

$s_i$.definition: The surplus inventory at the end of month $i$.

network simplex.definition: A specialized version of the simplex method designed to solve network flow problems, leveraging the network structure for efficiency.

$b_i$.definition: Supply at node i in a network flow problem.

$c_{ij}$.definition: Cost of flow along the edge from node i to node j in a network flow problem.

$b_j$.definition: Demand at node j in a network flow problem.

spanning tree.definition: A subgraph of a network that includes all nodes and forms a tree (no cycles). In the context of network simplex, it represents a basic feasible solution.

finding a feasible solution on a spannin.term: Finding a feasible solution on a spanning tree
finding a feasible solution on a spannin.definition: The problem of identifying an initial feasible solution for a network flow problem by selecting a spanning tree within the network.

cycle identification.definition: Identify the cycle created by adding the entering arc to the spanning tree.

flow adjustment.definition: Adjust flow along the cycle to maintain feasibility.

leaving arc selection.definition: Select the arc that reaches zero flow first when adjusting flow along the cycle.
